jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

Scotch is building the next-generation operating system for beverage alcohol retailers — combining POS, payments, back office, and e-commerce into a platform purpose-built for liquor stores.

We’re modernizing one of the oldest industries in the world: the $1.6T beverage alcohol market. Our platform helps retailers run more efficiently through streamlined payments, inventory management, reporting, and day-to-day operations.

Our founders came from Skupos (acquired 2023) and Drizly (acquired by Uber). We've raised $28M from VMG Partners, First Round, Lerer Hippeau, Watchfire, and Toba Capital, with angels including the founder of Drizly and early Toast executives. Forbes has recognized Scotch as a leader in liquor retail tech. We closed a $20M Series A in 2026 off 500%+ YoY growth and $1B+ in processed payment volume.

Position Overview

We're looking for a Product Manager to own the in-store experience at Scotch — the Android point-of-sale terminal our merchants use to ring up every sale. It's the part of our product customers touch every day, and it's where we're most visibly right or wrong.

This is a hands-on role with real autonomy. You'll own the terminal end-to-end: spending time in stores watching people use it, setting direction for what we build, and working with engineering to ship it. You'll be the person who knows how the device actually behaves in a busy store on a Friday night, not just how it behaves in a demo.

We're a small product org. That means you'll make calls without a committee, and you'll be accountable for the ones that turn out wrong. You won't be setting strategy alone — but you'll have a real hand in shaping it, and the closest view of the customer of anyone in the room.

Key Responsibilities

- Own the roadmap for our point-of-sale app. Shape the direction for the register experience with us, turn it into a sequence of releases, and defend the tradeoffs to people who'd rather ship something else.

- Prioritize across merchant escalations, platform work, and the long-horizon bets that never feel urgent. Partner closely with engineering on scoping and sequencing, including the parts where the right answer is "not yet."

- Spend real time in stores with merchants and their staff. Learn what they need, what they actually do, and where those two differ, and bring back things nobody would have found in a ticket.

- Translate messy, conflicting merchant input into a clear direction, and hold that direction when the inputs keep changing. Write requirements that describe the problem and the outcome, not the implementation.

- Make sure the app holds up in a real store: the peripherals it talks to, the network it doesn't always have, and the pace it has to keep up with.

- Own releases end to end. Decide what ships and what waits, how it rolls out, and who needs to know before it lands. Own the response when something goes wrong on a device that's already sitting on a counter.

- Serve as the product point of contact for support, onboarding, and go-to-market on anything happening at the register. That includes writing the release notes that keep those teams ahead of what's shipping, and eventually getting them in front of merchants too.

- Define what success looks like before we build, then go look. Instrument the work, watch adoption, and say plainly when something didn't land.

- Raise the bar around you on how we write, how we decide, and how we talk to merchants.

Qualifications & Skills

- 5+ years of product management experience.

- Experience owning a native mobile app as a product surface, heavily preferred. That means setting a release cadence, rolling changes out to devices already in use, and deciding what to do when a version in the field is broken.

- Our app deploys to managed devices, not through an app store, so fleet or MDM experience matters more here than consumer app publishing. This is the hardest skill on this list for us to teach.

- A track record of being the only person accountable for a decision, with no one reviewing your work before it shipped. This matters more to us than company size or whether you've worked at a startup.

- A consistent habit of direct customer contact. You've sat with users, watched them work, and changed your mind because of what you saw. In this role, that happens in person at merchants' stores, not over video calls.

- Sound judgment you can explain. You can walk through a call you got wrong, ideally one you caught yourself before anyone pointed it out.

- Experience running several workstreams at once and making the tradeoffs between them yourself, not only executing on priorities someone else set.

- Clear communication for different audiences. You can write a spec an engineer can build from, then explain the same decision to a merchant, a support lead, and an executive.

Nice to Haves

- Experience with hardware, peripherals, or devices deployed in the field — printers, scanners, card readers, or anything that fails in ways software alone doesn't

- Products built for environments where the user is busy, interrupted, and has a customer waiting

- Retail or point-of-sale background, particularly with independent or small-format merchants

- Payments experience — tender types, reconciliation, or dual pricing

- Fluency with AI tools in your daily workflow

Compensation & Benefits

- Compensation: The anticipated base salary range for this position is $150,000–$170,000. Individual offers are based on a variety of factors, including experience, skills, qualifications, and internal equity.

- Competitive equity package

- Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage

- Unlimited flexible PTO

Why Scotch?

- Real ownership, early. You'd be the product owner for the register, the part of Scotch merchants use every day, and your decisions would ship without layers of review.

- A vertical that's been underserved. Beverage alcohol retailers have been stuck with generic or outdated POS systems. We build specifically for them, across 18 states and counting.

- Well-backed and still early. We raised a $20M Series A from VMG Partners, First Round Capital, Lerer Hippeau, Toba Capital, and Watchfire Ventures, and we're small enough that one person changes the trajectory.

- A team that holds a high bar. We run on trust, a bias for action, and sharpening each other's steel. You'd get candor and autonomy, not micromanagement.

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

Scotch is building the next-generation operating system for beverage alcohol retailers — combining POS, payments, back office, and e-commerce into a platform purpose-built for liquor stores.

We’re modernizing one of the oldest industries in the world: the $1.6T beverage alcohol market. Our platform helps retailers run more efficiently through streamlined payments, inventory management, reporting, and day-to-day operations.

Our founders came from Skupos (acquired 2023) and Drizly (acquired by Uber). We've raised $28M from VMG Partners, First Round, Lerer Hippeau, Watchfire, and Toba Capital, with angels including the founder of Drizly and early Toast executives. Forbes has recognized Scotch as a leader in liquor retail tech. We closed a $20M Series A in 2026 off 500%+ YoY growth and $1B+ in processed payment volume.

Position Overview

We're looking for a Product Manager to help drive the vision of the Scotch back office - the web application where our merchants run their business. The register is where a sale happens; the back office is where the business gets managed, and it's where Scotch can help our merchants make better revenue-driving decisions.

This is a hands-on role with real autonomy. You'll work with other product managers to build and execute the back office vision end-to-end. In particular, you'll focus on the product catalog, ordering and receiving, and other inventory management features.

We're also building AI into the core of the product to help merchants get through the tedious, error-prone parts of running inventory and books faster, without giving up control or trust. You'll help decide where AI genuinely earns its place in a SaaS workflow, and where it doesn't.

We're a small product org. That means you'll make calls without a committee, and you'll be accountable for the ones that turn out wrong. You won't be setting strategy alone but you'll have a real hand in shaping it, and have one of the closest views of the customer in the room.

- Own the merchant operations roadmap for the back-office web app, turning direction into a sequence of releases and deciding what goes into each one

- Own core inventory and back-office workflows: creating and editing products, receiving, ordering, transfers, pricing, and shelf labels

- Gather requirements from merchants and their staff to understand what they need, what they actually do, and the frequent gap between the two

- Execute on our AI feature strategy within the back office: which problems it should solve, how it earns merchant trust, and how we measure whether it's working

- Serve as the product point of contact for support, onboarding, and go-to-market on anything in the back-office feature areas you own

- Shape the direction for the back office with us, then own the decisions inside it and defend those tradeoffs to people who'd rather ship something else

- Translate messy, conflicting merchant input into a clear direction, and hold that direction when the inputs keep changing

- Write requirements that describe the problem and the outcome, not the implementation

- Design for organizational scale, not just data scale: the same workflow has to work for a solo owner and for a multi-location tenant with layered roles, delegated access, and different people responsible for different things

- Decide where AI belongs in a workflow (what it drafts, what it automates, where it must show its work, and where a human stays in the loop) and define how we evaluate quality before we ship

- Prioritize across merchant escalations, platform work, and the long-horizon bets that never feel urgent

- Partner closely with engineering on scoping and sequencing, including when the right answer is "not yet"

- Coordinate releases end to end: what goes in, how it rolls out, who needs to know before it lands, and what happens when it doesn't go to plan

- Define what success looks like before we build, instrument the work, watch adoption, and say plainly when something didn't land

- Spend real time with merchants and their back-office staff, and bring back what nobody would have found in a ticket

- Raise the bar on how we write, how we decide, and how we talk to merchants

Qualifications & Skills

- 5+ years of product management experience, with a track record of owning product areas from discovery through launch and iteration.

- Experience managing complex, data-heavy web applications strongly preferred, including evolving established workflows that customers rely on daily.

- Experience bringing AI-powered features from concept to production within an established SaaS product, with an understanding of quality evaluation, user trust, and where human oversight is needed.

- Experience designing administrative workflows and multi-tenant products, including roles, permissions, approvals, audit needs, and support for multiple locations and teams.

- Demonstrated autonomy and accountability, with experience making product decisions independently and taking ownership of the outcomes.

- Strong customer discovery skills, with a habit of observing users, testing assumptions, and incorporating findings into product decisions. Enthusiasm for onsite research with store owners, managers, buyers, and bookkeepers.

- Sound product judgment and self-awareness, with the ability to explain tradeoffs, recognize when a decision isn’t working, and adjust course.

- Strong prioritization skills, with experience managing multiple workstreams and balancing customer needs, platform investments, and longer-term opportunities.

- Clear written and verbal communication, including actionable product requirements and the ability to explain decisions to engineering, customers, cross-functional partners, and executives.

Nice to Haves

- Prior product experience in accounting, finance, or inventory management products — anything where accuracy, reconciliation, and an audit trail matter to the user. Bonus points if you're fond of FIFO

- Experience with purchasing, receiving, invoicing, or accounts-payable workflows

- Retail, distribution, or point-of-sale background, particularly with independent or small-format merchants

- Comfort working with data directly — writing or reading SQL to answer your own product questions

- Fluency with AI tools in your daily workflow

Compensation & Benefits

- Compensation: The anticipated base salary range for this position is $150,000 – $170,000. Individual offers are based on a variety of factors, including experience, skills, qualifications, and internal equity.

- Competitive equity package

- Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage

- Unlimited flexible PTO

Why Scotch?

- Build products that make a tangible difference . Help liquor store owners simplify daily operations, manage inventory, and make better business decisions.

- Have real ownership and influence . Join a small product team where you’ll shape the roadmap, work directly with merchants, and own meaningful product decisions from discovery through launch.

- Put AI to work on real problems . Help define how AI fits into everyday merchant workflows, reducing tedious work while preserving user control and trust.

- Join a company with strong momentum . Following a $20M Series A in 2026, 500%+ year-over-year growth, and $1B+ in processed payment volume, help modernize the $1.6T beverage alcohol industry alongside an experienced founding team.
